title: Apparently he's busy
goal: At the office, Maryam asks whether the client has replied to your proposal; answer without promising more than you know
tip: Hedge before the clause: iẓ-ẓāhir innah mashghūl 'apparently he's busy'; ḥasab ʿilmi, lil-ḥīn ma radd 'as far as I know, he hasn't replied yet'. Guess, then soften it: akhammin innhum biywaggʿūn, bas ma aẓman 'I'd guess they'll sign, but I can't promise'.
grammar: hedging: iẓ-ẓāhir inn, ḥasab ʿilmi, akhammin, ma aẓman
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. العميل رد على العرض اللي طرشناه؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. il-ʿamīl radd ʿala l-ʿarẓ illi ṭarrashnāh?
Morning. Has the client replied about the proposal we sent?
B
صباح النور. حسب علمي، للحين ما رد
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. ḥasab ʿilmi, lil-ḥīn ma radd
Morning. As far as I know, he hasn't replied yet.
A
غريبة! قال لنا بيرد قبل الويكند. الإدارة تسألني، وأنا مب مرتاحة
gharība! gāl-lna biyrudd gabil il-wīkind. il-idāra tisʼalni, w ana mub mirtāḥa
Odd! He told us he'd reply before the weekend. The management keeps asking me, and I'm uneasy.
B
الظاهر إنه مشغول هالأيام، أو يمكن ما له مزاج
iẓ-ẓāhir innah mashghūl hal-ayyām, aw yimkin ma lah mizāj
Apparently he's busy these days, or maybe he's not in the mood.
A
يمكن. بس بيوقعون العقد ولّا لا؟ شو تخمن؟
yimkin. bas biywaggʿūn il-ʿagid walla la? shu tkhammin?
Maybe. But will they sign the contract or not? What's your guess?
B
أخمن إنهم بيوقعون، بس ما أضمن
akhammin innhum biywaggʿūn, bas ma aẓman
I'd guess they'll sign, but I can't promise.
A
بس ردهم الأخير كان غامض. طلبوا خصم ونسخة من كل شي
bas radd-hum il-akhīr kān ghāmiẓ. ṭalabaw khaṣim w nuskha min kill shay
But their last reply was vague. They asked for a discount and a copy of everything.
B
مب متأكد، بس الظاهر إن المشروع عجبهم
mub mitʼakkid, bas iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-mashrūʿ ʿajabhum
I'm not sure, but it looks like they liked the project.
A
زين. شو الحل؟ إذا ما ردوا لين الأحد، بتصل فيهم بنفسي
zēn. shu l-ḥall? idha ma raddaw lēn il-aḥad, battaṣil fīhum b-nafsi
OK. So what do we do? If they haven't replied by Sunday, I'll call them myself.
B
فكرة زينة. بس إذا طلبوا تأجيل، هذي هي المشكلة
fikra zēna. bas idha ṭalabaw taʼjīl, hādhi hiya l-mushkila
Good idea. But if they ask for a delay, that's the real problem.
items: apparently, it looks like (+ a clause)
with a pronoun: iẓ-ẓāhir innah (he, it), iẓ-ẓāhir innhum (they)
what's your guess? shu tkhammin? (شو تخمن؟) to a man
his mood: mizājah (مزاجه); he's not in the mood: ma lah mizāj (ما له مزاج); I'm not in the mood: māli mizāj (مالي مزاج)
culture: In everyday Emirati speech, in shāʼ allāh does several jobs: a plan that's already made, a polite hope, or, when it's drawn out (in shāʼ allāāh…), a gentle way of not promising. Listen to the tone, and to whether a time or a next step comes with it.

title: Something's definitely up
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, Rāshid can't stop smiling at his phone; guess with his father what has happened
tip: Guess from what you can see: wāẓiḥ innah farḥān 'he's clearly happy', ṭāyir min il-farḥa 'over the moon'; akīd fī shay 'something's definitely up'. Push a guess away: ashukk innah min il-madrasa 'I doubt it's about school'.
grammar: guessing from evidence: wāẓiḥ inn, akīd fī shay, ashukk inn
dialogue: A
شوف راشد، من الصبح يبتسم وعيونه تلمع، ومزاجه حلو
shūf Rāshid, min iṣ-ṣubḥ yibtisim w ʿyūnah tilmaʿ, w mizājah ḥilu
Look at Rāshid: since this morning he's been smiling, his eyes shining, and he's in a great mood.
B
واضح إنه فرحان، يا عمي. طاير من الفرحة!
wāẓiḥ innah farḥān, yā ʿammi. ṭāyir min il-farḥa!
He's clearly happy, uncle. Over the moon!
A
أكيد في شي. بس شو؟ هالولد يخفي شي، وكلامه غامض
akīd fī shay. bas shu? hal-walad yikhfi shay, w kalāmah ghāmiẓ
Something's definitely up. But what? This boy's hiding something, and he's being vague.
B
الظاهر إن النتايج طلعت؟
iẓ-ẓāhir inn in-natāyij ṭilʿat?
Looks like the results have come out?
A
لا، حسب علمي النتايج بعد أسبوعين. والمدرسة خلصت
la, ḥasab ʿilmi n-natāyij baʿd usbūʿēn. w il-madrasa khilṣat
No, as far as I know the results are in two weeks. And school's over.
B
عيل أشك إنه من المدرسة. في احتمال كبير إنه الكورس اللي قدم عليه
ʿayal ashukk innah min il-madrasa. fī iḥtimāl kbīr innah il-kōrs illi gaddam ʿalēh
Then I doubt it's about school. There's a good chance it's the course he applied for.
A
أي كورس؟ أنا مب متأكد إنه قال لي عن أي كورس
ay kōrs? ana mub mitʼakkid innah gāl-li ʿan ay kōrs
What course? I'm not sure he told me about any course.
B
كورس برمجة في الصيف. ساعدته في الطلب الشهر اللي طاف
kōrs barmaja fi ṣ-ṣēf. sāʿadtah fi ṭ-ṭalab ish-shahar illi ṭāf
A programming course in the summer. I helped him with the application last month.
A
راشد! تعال... يقول قبلوه! والله ما قال لأحد
Rāshid! taʿāl... ygūl gibalōh! wallāh ma gāl l-aḥad
Rāshid! Come here... He says they've accepted him! He really didn't tell anyone.
B
ما شاء الله عليه! كنت متأكد إنه بيدخل
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēh! kint mitʼakkid innah biyidkhil
Good for him! I was sure he'd get in.
items: I doubt (that) he…, I doubt (that) it…
a course (a short course, not a degree)

title: Nothing official yet
goal: At the office, Maryam has heard the company may keep on two interns next year; find out where the news came from and how sure it is
tip: Ask where news comes from: shu l-maṣdar? Then say how solid it is: ma fī shay rasmi 'nothing's official'; mithil ma simaʿt 'from what I heard'. Don't get carried away: la tifraḥ wāyid, lēn yṣīr rasmi.
grammar: reporting what you've heard: shu l-maṣdar?, mithil ma simaʿt, ma fī shay rasmi
dialogue: A
عندي لك خبر. يقولون إن الشركة بتثبت ثنين من المتدربين السنة الياية
ʿindi lak khabar. ygūlūn inn ish-sharika bitthabbit thnēn min il-mitdarrbīn is-sana l-yāya
I've got news for you. They say the company will keep on two of the interns next year.
B
لا والله! منو قال لج؟ شو المصدر؟
la wallāh! minu gāl-lich? shu l-maṣdar?
No way! Who told you? What's the source?
A
سارة من شؤون الموظفين. بس الخبر تسرب، وللحين غامض
Sāra min shuʼūn il-muwaẓẓafīn. bas il-khabar tsarrab, w lil-ḥīn ghāmiẓ
Sāra from HR. But the news leaked, and it's still vague.
B
يعني الخبر أكيد؟
yaʿni l-khabar akīd?
So the news is certain?
A
لا، للحين ما في شي رسمي. ولا تصدق القيل والقال هني
la, lil-ḥīn ma fī shay rasmi. w la tṣaddig il-gīl w il-gāl hni
No, nothing's official yet. And don't believe all the gossip here.
B
حلو! بس مثل ما سمعتي، منو بيختارون؟ شو تخمنين؟
ḥilu! bas mithil ma simaʿti, minu biyikhtārūn? shu tkhammnīn?
Great! But from what you heard, who will they choose? What's your guess?
A
الظاهر إن اللي شغلهم زين. ويمكن بعد اللي عندهم واسطة!
iẓ-ẓāhir inn illi shughulhum zēn. w yimkin baʿad illi ʿind-hum wāsṭa!
Apparently the ones whose work is good. And maybe also the ones with connections!
B
زين. بس أشك إنهم بيختاروني. ما بفرح لين يصير رسمي
zēn. bas ashukk innhum biyikhtārūni. ma bafraḥ lēn yṣīr rasmi
OK. But I doubt they'll choose me. I won't celebrate until it's official.
A
لا تفرح وايد. بس سارة تقول التثبيت ييي ويا مكافأة
la tifraḥ wāyid. bas Sāra tgūl it-tathbīt yiyi wiyya mukāfaʼa
Don't get your hopes up. But Sāra says being kept on comes with a bonus.
B
مكافأة؟ لو صج، بكون طاير من الفرحة!
mukāfaʼa? lō ṣij, bakūn ṭāyir min il-farḥa!
A bonus? If it's true, I'll be over the moon!
items: being taken on permanently (in a job)

title: Fahad's bet
goal: Video call: Fahad, on a few months' work posting in Kuwait, asks if Sēf knows he's flying back for Bū Rāshid's farewell dinner; weigh up his Kuwaiti guesses
tip: Fahad guesses the Kuwaiti way, with chūd: chūd yadri 'maybe he knows'. You hedge your own way: ma astabʿid innah yiktishif 'I wouldn't be surprised if he finds out', or deny it: ma ʿindah khabar 'he has no idea'.
grammar: epistemic chūd (Kuwait, recognise); ma astabʿid, ma ʿindah khabar
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak?
Hi there! How are you?
B
هلا بك! زين الحمد لله، وانت؟
hala bik! zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh, w inta?
Hi! Fine, thank God, and you?
A
تمام. اسمع، مثل ما سمعت بو راشد بيسوي عشا يوم الخميس. سيف يدري إني جاي؟
tamām. ismaʿ, mithil ma simaʿt Bū Rāshid biysawwi ʿasha yōm il-khamīs. Sēf yadri inni jāy?
Great. Listen, from what I heard, Bū Rāshid's giving a dinner on Thursday. Does Sēf know I'm coming?
B
لا، ما عنده خبر. محد قال له
la, ma ʿindah khabar. maḥḥad gāl-lah
No, he has no idea. Nobody's told him.
A
جود يدري ويسوي نفسه ما يدري! سيف فطين، ترا
chūd yadri w ysawwi nafsah ma yadri! Sēf faṭīn, tara
Maybe he knows and he's pretending not to! Sēf's sharp, you know.
B
صح ذكي، بس أشك إنه يدري. هو على نياته
ṣaḥḥ dhaki, bas ashukk innah yadri. huwa ʿala nyātah
True, he's clever, but I doubt he knows. He's too trusting.
A
جود أمه قالت له. الظاهر إن الأمهات ما يقدرون يخفون شي
chūd ummah gālat-lah. iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-ummahāt ma yigdarūn yikhfūn shay
Maybe his mother told him. It seems mums can't hide anything.
B
لا، أم سيف تبيها مفاجأة. واضح إنها متحمسة
la, Umm Sēf tabīha mufājaʼa. wāẓiḥ innha mitḥammsa
No, Umm Sēf wants it to be a surprise. She's clearly excited.
A
زين، عيل ما راح أقول له شي. بس جود أتأخر شوي، عندي مشوار
zēn, ʿayal ma rāḥ agūl-lah shay. bas chūd atʼakhkhar shwayy, ʿindi mishwār
OK, then I won't say a thing to him. But I might be a bit late; I've got an errand to run.
B
ما أستبعد إنه يكتشف، بس ما عليه. المهم إنك تيي
ma astabʿid innah yiktishif, bas ma ʿalēh. il-muhimm innak tiyi
I wouldn't be surprised if he finds out, but never mind. The main thing is that you come.
items: maybe he knows, he might know (Kuwait)
chūd + a verb: chūd atʼakhkhar (جود أتأخر) 'I might be late'; (recognise)
naive, trusting, he takes things at face value
about a woman: ʿala nyāt-ha (على نياتها)
sharp, quick on the uptake (a man)
culture: Kuwaiti speakers have a word for a guess, chūd (جود), that the Emirati cast doesn't use: chūd yadri 'maybe he knows', chūd atʼakhkhar 'I might be late'. Learn to hear it from Fahad and Nūra; for your own guesses, keep to yimkin, iẓ-ẓāhir and ma astabʿid.

title: Too good to be true
goal: At a karak stand, Sēf shows you an ad promising easy money from home; say why you doubt it, without making fun of him
tip: Doubt politely, then give a reason: ashukk innah ṣij 'I doubt it's true', shaklah khidʿa 'it looks like a trick'; kalām fāẓi 'that's nonsense' is for friends. Reason with lō: lō kān ṣij, chān killna sawwēnāh 'if it were true, we'd all have done it'.
grammar: doubt and disbelief: ashukk inn, shaklah khidʿa, kalām fāẓi
dialogue: A
شوف هالإعلان! يقولون تربح خمسة آلاف في الأسبوع من البيت
shūf hal-iʿlān! ygūlūn tirbaḥ khamsat ālāf fi l-usbūʿ min il-bēt
Look at this ad! They say you earn five thousand a week from home.
B
خمسة آلاف؟ أشك إنه صج. شكله خدعة
khamsat ālāf? ashukk innah ṣij. shaklah khidʿa
Five thousand? I doubt it's true. It looks like a trick.
A
ليش؟ حاطين صور ناس ربحوا، والأرباح مضمونة على كلامهم
lēsh? ḥāṭṭīn ṣuwar nās ribḥaw, w il-arbāḥ maẓmūna ʿala kalāmhum
Why? They've put up photos of people who made money, and the profits are guaranteed, so they say.
B
يا ريّال، هذا كلام فاضي. شو المصدر؟ الصور وهمية
yā rayyāl, hādha kalām fāẓi. shu l-maṣdar? iṣ-ṣuwar wahmiyya
Come on, man, that's nonsense. What's the source? The photos are fake.
A
بس يبون مية درهم بس عشان تبدا
bas yabūn miyat dirham bas ʿashān tibda
But they only want a hundred dirhams for you to start.
B
هني المشكلة. هذا فخ، ما في شي ببلاش
hni l-mushkila. hādha fakhkh, ma fī shay b-balāsh
That's the problem. It's a trap; nothing's for free.
A
يمكن صج. في احتمال كبير، ما تدري
yimkin ṣij. fī iḥtimāl kbīr, ma tadri
Maybe it's true. There's a good chance; you never know.
B
لو كان صج، جان كلنا سويناه. لا تخلي الطمع يغلبك
lō kān ṣij, chān killna sawwēnāh. la tkhalli ṭ-ṭamaʿ yighlbak
If it were true, we'd all have done it. Don't let greed get the better of you.
A
هههه، معك حق. الظاهر إن الإعلان نصب، ولا تقول إني ساذج!
hahaha, maʿak ḥagg. iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-iʿlān naṣib, w la tgūl inni sādhij!
Haha, you're right. It looks like the ad's a scam, and don't call me gullible!
B
انت على نياتك. لا تحط فيه درهم
inta ʿala nyātak. la tḥuṭṭ fīh dirham
You're too trusting. Don't put a dirham into it.
items: you earn, you make money; you win (to a man)
a feminine noun or plural things: wahmiyya (وهمية)
task: This week: search YouTube for «سوالف» or «بودكاست إماراتي». Listen for 10 minutes and note every time a speaker hedges or doubts (yimkin, iẓ-ẓāhir, ashukk, ma aẓunn, ḥasab ʿilmi). Write down three sentences around them. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait); if you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.

title: He told me himself
goal: On the metro with Sēf, you disagree about which night Bū Rāshid's dinner is; back up your version by saying where you heard it
tip: Say how you know: gālha-li b-nafsah 'he told me himself'. Ask for proof: min wēn simaʿt? shu d-dalīl? And back yourself: idha ṭilaʿt ghalṭān 'if I turn out to be wrong', ana mitʼakkid miya bil-miya 'I'm a hundred percent sure'.
grammar: certainty and its source: b-nafsah, shu d-dalīl?, miya bil-miya
dialogue: A
عشا عمي يوم الجمعة، صح؟
ʿasha ʿammi yōm il-jumʿa, ṣaḥḥ?
My uncle's dinner is on Friday, right?
B
لا، يوم الخميس. أضمن لك
la, yōm il-khamīs. aẓman-lak
No, on Thursday. Take it from me.
A
انت غلطان. أنا متيقن إنها الجمعة
inta ghalṭān. ana mitayaqqin innha l-jumʿa
You're wrong. I'm positive (ironic) it's Friday.
B
من وين سمعت؟ شو الدليل؟
min wēn simaʿt? shu d-dalīl?
Where did you hear that? What's your proof?
A
ما أذكر بالضبط. أخمن إنه راشد، بس مب متأكد
ma adhkur biẓ-ẓabṭ. akhammin innah Rāshid, bas mub mitʼakkid
I don't remember exactly. I'd guess it was Rāshid, but I'm not sure.
B
عمك قالها لي بنفسه في المجلس، وهذي حجتي
ʿammak gālha-li b-nafsah fi l-majlis, w hādhi ḥijjti
Your uncle told me himself, in the majlis, and that's my case.
A
كلام فاضي! أشك إنه الخميس. وين البرهان؟
kalām fāẓi! ashukk innah il-khamīs. wēn il-burhān?
Rubbish! I doubt it's Thursday. Where's the proof? (ironic)
B
إذا طلعت غلطان، أعزمك على كرك. بس الظاهر إنك بتخسر
idha ṭilaʿt ghalṭān, aʿazmak ʿala karak. bas iẓ-ẓāhir innak bitikhsar
If I turn out to be wrong, I'll buy you karak. But it looks like you're going to lose.
A
اتفقنا، رهان! بطرش لعمي، وهو يشهد منو الصح
ittafagna, rihān! baṭarrish l-ʿammi, w huwa yishhad minu ṣ-ṣaḥḥ
Deal, it's a bet! I'll message my uncle, and he can say who's right.
B
طرش. أنا متأكد مية بالمية، ورسالته مكتوب فيها الخميس
ṭarrish. ana mitʼakkid miya bil-miya, w risāltah maktūb fīha l-khamīs
Go ahead. I'm a hundred percent sure, and his message says Thursday.
items: what's your proof? shu d-dalīl? (شو الدليل؟)
your case: ḥijjtak (حجتك) to a man
I'm a witness: ana ashhad (أنا أشهد)

title: May God make it easy for him
goal: At Sēf's family home, with Bū Rāshid there and Sēf upstairs packing, Umm Sēf tells you she's worried about him going; answer her worry with blessings
tip: Wish someone well by asking God for it: allāh ysahhil ʿalēh 'may God make it easy for him', allāh yiktib-lah illi fīh il-khēr 'may God bring him what's best'. With ʿasa + a verb: ʿasāha tkūn sana khēr 'may it be a good year'.
grammar: optatives: allāh y- + wish; ʿasa + wish
dialogue: A
هلا يا وليدي، حياك الله. سيف فوق يرتب شنطته
hala yā wlēdi, ḥayyāk allāh. Sēf fōg yrattib shanṭtah
Hello, my son, welcome. Sēf's upstairs packing his suitcase.
B
الله يحييج يا خالتي. شحالج؟
allāh yḥayyīch yā khālti. shḥālich?
Thank you, auntie. How are you?
A
بخير الحمد لله. بس أنا قلقانة، الولد على نياته وبيسافر بعيد
b-khēr il-ḥamdu lillāh. bas ana galgāna, il-walad ʿala nyātah w biysāfir baʿīd
Fine, thank God. But I'm worried; the boy's so trusting, and he's going far away.
B
الله يسهل عليه، ويرده سالم غانم
allāh ysahhil ʿalēh, w yruddah sālim ghānim
May God make it easy for him, and bring him back safe and sound.
A
آمين. ادعي له يا وليدي، الرحلة طويلة
āmīn. idʿī-lah yā wlēdi, ir-riḥla ṭawīla
Amen. Pray for him, my son; it's a long journey.
B
أكيد بدعي له. أنا متأكد إنه مستعد
akīd badʿī-lah. ana mitʼakkid innah mistaʿidd
Of course I'll pray for him. I'm certain he's ready.
A
الله يحفظك. الظاهر إنه بيتعب أول، بس عساها تكون سنة خير عليه
allāh yiḥfaẓak. iẓ-ẓāhir innah biyitʿab awwal, bas ʿasāha tkūn sana khēr ʿalēh
God keep you. It looks like he'll struggle at first, but may it be a good year for him.
B
الله يكتب له اللي فيه الخير. انتي حنونة يا خالتي
allāh yiktib-lah illi fīh il-khēr. inti ḥanūna yā khālti
May God bring him what's best. You're so caring, auntie.
A
آمين يا رب... هذا هو نزل! عسى عمرك طويل، كنا نتكلم عنك
āmīn yā rabb... hādha huwa nizal! ʿasa ʿumrak ṭawīl, kinna nitkallam ʿannak
Amen... Here he is, he's come down! Speak of the devil, we were just talking about you.
B
هلا سيف! يلا، بساعدك في الشنطة
hala Sēf! yalla, basāʿdak fi sh-shanṭa
Hi Sēf! Come on, I'll help you with the suitcase.
items: to a woman: idʿī-lah (the same); I pray for him: adʿī-lah (أدعي له); I'll pray for him: badʿī-lah (بدعي له)
speak of the devil! (kindly; lit. may your life be long)
said to someone who turns up as you mention him; (recognise)
culture: Before a journey, many Arabic-speaking travellers say the travel prayer (duʿāʼ as-safar), asking God to protect them on the way. Here Umm Sēf and you add your own blessings: may God make it easy for him and bring him back safe.

title: God be pleased with you
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he thanks you for helping Rāshid with his course; take his thanks and bless him back
tip: An elder thanks you with a blessing: allāh yirẓa ʿalēk, allāh yisʿidak. Play it down (hādha aqall shay, hādha l-wājib) and bless him back: āmīn yā rabb, allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak. When he says mā gaṣṣart, the reply is still mā sawwēna shay.
grammar: optatives as thanks: allāh yisʿidak, allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak, allāh yhannīh
dialogue: A
حياك الله يا ولدي! راشد ما وقف يسولف عنك
ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi! Rāshid ma wigaf ysōlif ʿannak
Welcome, son! Rāshid hasn't stopped talking about you.
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. شحالك؟
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. shḥālak?
Thank you, uncle. How are you?
A
بخير الله يسلمك. الله يرضى عليك، ساعدته في طلب الكورس
b-khēr allāh ysallmak. allāh yirẓa ʿalēk, sāʿadtah fi ṭalab il-kōrs
Fine, thank you. God bless you, you helped him with the course application.
B
هذا أقل شي، هذا الواجب يا عمي
hādha aqall shay, hādha l-wājib yā ʿammi
It's the least I could do, uncle; it's my duty.
A
لا والله، تعبت وياه وايد. الله يسعدك مثل ما فرحتنا
la wallāh, tiʿabt wiyyāh wāyid. allāh yisʿidak mithil ma farraḥtna
No, really, you went to a lot of trouble for him. May God make you happy, as you've made us happy.
B
آمين يا رب. أنا ممنون لك يا عمي، الله يطول عمرك
āmīn yā rabb. ana mamnūn lak yā ʿammi, allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak
Amen. I'm grateful to you, uncle. God give you a long life.
A
ويقول إنك عطيته اللابتوب حقك؟ والدليل، شايله وياه الحين
w ygūl innak ʿaṭētah il-lābtōb ḥaggak? w id-dalīl, shāylah wiyyāh il-ḥīn
And he says you gave him your laptop? And here's the proof: he's carrying it around now.
B
هيه، عندي واحد يديد. أنا متأكد إنه يحتاجه
hē, ʿindi wāḥid yidīd. ana mitʼakkid innah yiḥtājah
Yes, I've got a new one. I'm sure he needs it.
A
الله يخلف عليك، والله يجبر بخاطرك. ما قصرت والله
allāh yikhlif ʿalēk, w allāh yijbur b-khāṭrak. mā gaṣṣart wallāh
May God repay you, and may God be good to you. You've been so kind, truly.
B
ما سوينا شي يا عمي. الله يهنيه، وأدعي له بالتوفيق
mā sawwēna shay yā ʿammi. allāh yhannīh, w adʿī-lah bit-tawfīg
It was nothing, uncle. I hope he enjoys it, and I pray he does well.
items: God bless you (warm thanks, usually from an older person) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yirẓa ʿalēch (الله يرضى عليج); (recognise)
(my) duty, the least I could do
it's my duty: hādha l-wājib (هذا الواجب)
may he enjoy it (said of something given to him)
to the person himself: allāh yhannīk (الله يهنيك)
may God repay you (for what you've given or spent) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yikhlif ʿalēch; (recognise)
may God be good to you, bless you for your kindness (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yijbur b-khāṭrich; (recognise)

title: Come on, keep going!
goal: On a video call, Rāshid says his programming course is too hard after one week and he wants to quit; talk him into carrying on
tip: Urge a friend on with commands: shidd ḥēlak! 'come on, keep at it!', inta gadd-ha 'you can do it'. Stop him with la + verb: la tōgaf il-ḥīn 'don't stop now', la tgārin nafsak fīhum 'don't compare yourself with them'.
grammar: urging: shidd ḥēlak, inta gadd-ha, la + verb
dialogue: A
برو، الكورس صعب وايد. أفكر أطلع منه
brō, il-kōrs ṣaʿb wāyid. afakkir aṭlaʿ minnah
Bro, the course is really hard. I'm thinking of dropping out.
B
تطلع بعد أسبوع واحد؟ كلام فاضي!
tiṭlaʿ baʿd usbūʿ wāḥid? kalām fāẓi!
Drop out after one week? Rubbish!
A
مليت! كل يوم كود، وراسي بينفجر
mallēt! kill yōm kōd, w rāsi biyinfijir
I'm fed up! Code every day, and my head's going to explode.
B
عادي، أول أسبوع دوم صعب. والأيام تمر بسرعة
ʿādi, awwal usbūʿ dōm ṣaʿb. w il-ayyām tmurr b-surʿa
That's normal; the first week's always hard. And the days go by fast.
A
بس الشباب الثانيين أشطر مني
bas ish-shabāb ith-thānyīn ashṭar minni
But the other guys are better than me.
B
لا تقارن نفسك فيهم. شد حيلك!
la tgārin nafsak fīhum. shidd ḥēlak!
Don't compare yourself with them. Come on, keep at it!
A
وإذا ما فهمت شي؟ شو الحل؟
w idha ma fhimt shay? shu l-ḥall?
And if I don't understand something? What do I do then?
B
اسأل، وخذها خطوة خطوة. هذا تحدي، وانت قدها
isʼal, w khidhha khaṭwa khaṭwa. hādha taḥaddi, w inta gadd-ha
Ask, and take it step by step. It's a challenge, and you can do it.
A
زين، ما بطلع. تسلم برو!
zēn, ma baṭlaʿ. tislam brō!
OK, I won't drop out. Thanks a lot, bro!
B
الله يسلمك. لا توقف الحين. كمل الشهر، ولا تفشلني!
allāh ysallmak. la tōgaf il-ḥīn. kammil ish-shahar, w la tfashshilni!
You're welcome. Don't stop now. Finish the month, and don't let me down!
items: come on, keep at it, put your back into it (to a man)
to a woman: shiddi ḥēlich (شدي حيلج); to a group: shiddu ḥēlkum (شدوا حيلكم)
you can do it, you're up to it (to a man)
to a woman: inti gadd-ha (انتي قدها)
to a woman: la tgārnīn nafsich (لا تقارنين نفسج)

title: Let's begin, with God's blessing
goal: At the office, Maryam starts a new project with the team; get everyone going, share out the work and answer her good wishes
tip: Start a job together: tawakkalna ʿala llāh or ʿala barakat illāh 'off we go'. Urge with let's: khal ngassim ish-shughul, yalla nibda; urge a group with the -u ending: shiddu ḥēlkum!
grammar: hortatives: tawakkalna, ʿala barakat illāh, khal, yalla + verb
dialogue: A
يلا يا جماعة، توكلنا على الله. المشروع اليديد يبدا اليوم
yalla yā jamāʿa, tawakkalna ʿala llāh. il-mashrūʿ il-yidīd yibda l-yōm
Right, everyone, let's get going. The new project starts today.
B
على بركة الله. شو أول شي؟
ʿala barakat illāh. shu awwal shay?
Off we go. What comes first?
A
المهلة لين الخميس، وما في وقت وايد. تحدي!
il-muhla lēn il-khamīs, w ma fī wagt wāyid. taḥaddi!
The deadline's Thursday, and there isn't much time. It's a challenge!
B
عيل خل نقسم الشغل بيننا. نبي تنظيم
ʿayal khal ngassim ish-shughul bēnna. nabi tanẓīm
Then let's split the work between us. We need some organisation.
A
فكرة زينة. انت خذ التقرير، وأنا آخذ العرض
fikra zēna. inta khidh it-taqrīr, w ana ākhidh il-ʿarẓ
Good idea. You take the report, and I'll take the presentation.
B
تمام. وانتو يا شباب، شدوا حيلكم!
tamām. w intu yā shabāb, shiddu ḥēlkum!
Fine. And you guys, put your backs into it!
A
وأبي أشوف طاقتكم وحماسكم. الظاهر إن العميل مستعيل
w abi ashūf ṭāqatkum w ḥamāskum. iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-ʿamīl mistaʿyil
And I want to see your energy and drive. It looks like the client's in a hurry.
B
لا تحاتين. حسب علمي كل شي ماشي، ويوم الخميس بنكون مخلصين
la tḥātīn. ḥasab ʿilmi kill shay māshi, w yōm il-khamīs binkūn mkhallṣīn
Don't worry. As far as I know everything's on track, and by Thursday we'll be done.
A
بالتوفيق للكل، وأبي أشوف إنجاز. الله يعطيكم العافية
bit-tawfīg lil-kill, w abi ashūf injāz. allāh yaʿṭīkum il-ʿāfya
Good luck, everyone; I want to see results. God give you strength.
B
الله يعافيج. الأيام تمر بسرعة، يلا نبدا!
allāh yʿāfīch. il-ayyām tmurr b-surʿa, yalla nibda!
Thank you. The days go by fast; let's get started!
items: let's get going, trusting in God (as you start something)
off we go, with God's blessing (as you start something)
your energy: ṭāqatkum (طاقتكم) to a group; (recognise)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor» or «مدرس لهجة إماراتية»), plan an imaginary group trip together for 10 minutes: who books what and by when. Start with tawakkalna ʿala llāh, split the jobs (kill wāḥid yākhidh…), urge them on once (shidd ḥēlak) and end with a wish (allāh ysahhil ʿalēk).

title: I swear I saw him!
goal: At a karak stand, you let slip to Sēf that you've just seen Fahad at Dubai Mall, though he's on a work posting in Kuwait; he won't believe you, so insist
tip: Insist with an oath and a fact: wallāh il-ʿaẓīm shiftah 'I swear I saw him'; huwa b-nafsah 'the man himself'. Sēf doubts: min jiddak? 'are you serious?'
grammar: insisting: wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, huwa b-nafsah, min jiddak?
dialogue: B
سيف، شفت فهد اليوم في دبي مول!
Sēf, shift Fahad il-yōm fi Dbayy Mōl!
Sēf, I saw Fahad today at Dubai Mall!
A
فهد؟ مستحيل، انت غلطان. فهد في الكويت، يتهيأ لك
Fahad? mustaḥīl, inta ghalṭān. Fahad fi l-Kwēt, yit-hayyaʼ-lak
Fahad? Impossible, you're wrong. Fahad's in Kuwait; you're imagining things.
B
والله العظيم شفته، عند النافورة
wallāh il-ʿaẓīm shiftah, ʿind in-nāfūra
I swear to God I saw him, by the fountain.
A
أشك إنه فهد. يمكن واحد يشبهه، أو يمكن عنده توأم!
ashukk innah Fahad. yimkin wāḥid yishbahah, aw yimkin ʿindah tawʼam!
I doubt it was Fahad. Maybe someone who looks like him, or maybe he's got a twin!
B
لا، هو بنفسه. حتى سلم علي من بعيد
la, huwa b-nafsah. ḥatta sallam ʿalay min baʿīd
No, it was him, the man himself. He even said hello to me from a distance.
A
من جدك؟ كان لابس كندورة؟ يمكن واحد ثاني، صدفة
min jiddak? kān lābis kandūra? yimkin wāḥid thāni, ṣudfa
Are you serious? Was he wearing a kandura? Maybe it was someone else, by coincidence.
B
ما أدري. بس أنا متأكد، والله العظيم
ma adri. bas ana mitʼakkid, wallāh il-ʿaẓīm
I don't know. But I'm certain, I swear to God.
A
انت تحب تمزح وايد، ترا. يمكن شفت شبح!
inta tḥibb timzaḥ wāyid, tara. yimkin shift shabaḥ!
You do like a joke, you know. Maybe you saw a ghost!
B
هالمرة ما أمزح. الظاهر إن فهد يخفي شي!
hal-marra ma amzaḥ. iẓ-ẓāhir inn Fahad yikhfi shay!
This time I'm not joking. It looks like Fahad's hiding something!
A
دقيقة... فهد طرش لي: أنا في الكويت، مشغول وايد. شفت؟ يتهيأ لك
digīga... Fahad ṭarrash-li: ana fi l-Kwēt, mashghūl wāyid. shift? yit-hayyaʼ-lak
Hang on... Fahad's messaged me: 'I'm in Kuwait, really busy.' See? You're imagining things.
items: to a woman: min jiddich? (من جدج؟); UAE also: min ṣidgak? (من صدقك؟)
culture: Wallāh 'by God' is everyday Gulf talk, used for 'really' or 'honestly'. You may also hear other oaths, such as ʿalay iṭ-ṭalāg: don't use them.

title: So much that I shut up
goal: At a café, Fahad (flown in from his Kuwait posting for the dinner, in secret) asks how Sēf took your news; tell him, and talk up the dinner that's coming
tip: Emphasise how far something went with lad-daraja inn: ẓiḥak ʿalay lad-daraja inni sikatt 'he laughed at me so much that I shut up'. Fahad's Kuwaiti emphasis is for recognising: kint gid ḥajazt 'I'd (really) booked'.
grammar: emphasis: lad-daraja inn, wala aḥla; Kuwaiti gid (recognise)
dialogue: A
سيف ما صدقك؟ يعني ما عنده خبر؟
Sēf ma ṣaddagak? yaʿni ma ʿindah khabar?
Sēf didn't believe you? So he has no idea?
B
لا، ضحك علي لدرجة إني سكت
la, ẓiḥak ʿalay lad-daraja inni sikatt
No, he laughed at me so much that I shut up.
A
زين سويت. ما كانت صدفة، أنا كنت قد حجزت من شهر
zēn sawwēt. ma kānat ṣudfa, ana kint gid ḥajazt min shahar
Good. It was no coincidence; I'd booked a whole month ago.
B
من شهر؟ من جدك؟ ليش تخبي علي؟
min shahar? min jiddak? lēsh tkhabbi ʿalay?
A month ago? Are you serious? Why hide it from me?
A
والله إني تعبت وأنا ساكت! خفت سيف يكتشف
wallāh inni tiʿabt w ana sākit! khift Sēf yiktishif
Honestly, keeping quiet wore me out! I was scared Sēf would find out.
B
هههه. بس العشا بيكون رهيب، ما تتخيل
hahaha. bas il-ʿasha biykūn rahīb, ma titkhayyal
Haha. But the dinner's going to be amazing, you can't imagine.
A
سمعت إن بو راشد مسوي ذبيحة، يعني خروف كامل؟
simaʿt inn Bū Rāshid msawwi dhbīḥa, yaʿni kharūf kāmil?
I heard Bū Rāshid's having a sheep done, a whole sheep?
B
هيه، وليمة كبيرة! طابخين أكل لدرجة إنه يكفي الفريج
hē, walīma kbīra! ṭābkhīn akil lad-daraja innah ykaffi l-firīj
Yes, a big feast! They're cooking so much food it'll feed the neighbourhood.
A
والله إنه كريم. الله يحفظه
wallāh innah karīm. allāh yiḥfaẓah
He really is generous. God keep him.
B
الله يحفظه. والله بتكون ليلة ولا أحلى
allāh yiḥfaẓah. wallāh bitkūn lēla wala aḥla
God keep him. It'll be a night like no other, honestly.
items: a slaughtered sheep, a whole sheep (cooked for guests)
a feast, a big dinner for guests
you hide, you keep (it) secret (to a man)
to a woman: tkhabbīn (تخبين); hide it from me: tkhabbi ʿalay

title: Nothing special, uncle
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he praises your Arabic and your work; accept the praise modestly and pass the credit on
tip: Take praise by playing it down: min dhōgak 'that's kind of you', bas mub dhāk iz-zōd 'but it's nothing special'. Pass the credit on: shay basīṭ, w Maryam sāʿadatni; ana mamnūn lakum 'I'm grateful to you all'.
grammar: understatement: mub dhāk iz-zōd, min dhōgak, shay basīṭ
dialogue: A
ما شاء الله تبارك الرحمن! سولفت مع الشواب في المجلس البارحة ساعة كاملة
mā shāʼ allāh tabārak ir-raḥmān! sōlaft maʿa sh-shuwwāb fi l-majlis il-bārḥa sāʿa kāmla
Mā shāʼ allāh, God bless! Last night in the majlis you chatted with the old men for a whole hour.
B
من ذوقك يا عمي. بس مب ذاك الزود
min dhōgak yā ʿammi. bas mub dhāk iz-zōd
That's kind of you, uncle. But it's nothing special.
A
لا والله، صرت تتكلم مثلنا
la wallāh, ṣirt titkallam mithilna
No, really, you speak like us now.
B
بعدني أغلط، لدرجة إن الشواب يضحكون! بس أحاول
baʿadni aghlaṭ, lad-daraja inn ish-shuwwāb yiẓḥakūn! bas aḥāwil
I still make mistakes, so many that the old men laugh! But I try.
A
الكل يغلط. العربي تحدي، والمهم إنك ما تستحي
il-kill yighlaṭ. il-ʿarabi taḥaddi, w il-muhimm innak ma tistiḥi
Everyone makes mistakes. Arabic's a challenge; what matters is you're not shy.
B
أنا ممنون لكم يا عمي. والله إني خجلان
ana mamnūn lakum yā ʿammi. wallāh inni khajlān
I'm grateful to you all, uncle. You're making me blush.
A
وسيف يقول إنك سويت التقرير في الشغل بروحك، ومريم بتعطيك مكافأة؟
w Sēf ygūl innak sawwēt it-taqrīr fi sh-shughul b-rūḥak, w Maryam bitʿaṭīk mukāfaʼa?
And Sēf says you did the report at work by yourself, and Maryam's going to give you a bonus?
B
شي بسيط، ومريم ساعدتني وايد فيه
shay basīṭ, w Maryam sāʿadatni wāyid fīh
It was nothing much, and Maryam helped me a lot with it.
A
تواضع منك! هذي أخلاق الرياييل، الله يسعدك
tawāẓuʿ minnak! hādhi akhlāg ir-ryāyīl, allāh yisʿidak
You're being modest! That's how a real man behaves, bless you.
B
الله يطول عمرك يا عمي. لا تخليني أصير مغرور!
allāh yṭawwil ʿumrak yā ʿammi. la tkhallīni aṣīr maghrūr!
God give you long life, uncle. Don't make me big-headed!
items: that's kind of you, how nice of you to say so (to a man)
to a woman: min dhōgich (من ذوقج)
nothing special, not all that great (UAE)
blessed be God (said with mā shāʼ allāh when praising)
culture: Praise in the Gulf usually comes with mā shāʼ allāh 'God has willed it', a reminder that good things come from God and a protection against envy and the evil eye. If someone praises you or your family and forgets it, others may say it for them.

title: It's no big deal
goal: At the office, Maryam has spilt coffee on her laptop just before a client meeting; calm her down and play the problem down
tip: Shrink a problem: mub sālfa 'it's no big deal', kill shay yhūn 'it's all manageable', mub awwal marra tṣīr 'it's not the first time it's happened'. To someone who's upset: khaffifi ʿala nafsich 'go easy on yourself'.
grammar: playing down: mub sālfa, kill shay yhūn, mub awwal marra
dialogue: A
يا ويلي! كبيت القهوة على اللابتوب، والاجتماع بعد ربع ساعة!
yā wēli! kabbēt il-gahwa ʿala l-lābtōb, w il-ijtimāʿ baʿd rubʿ sāʿa!
Oh no! I've spilt coffee on the laptop, and the meeting's in a quarter of an hour!
B
لا تحاتين، مب سالفة. الملفات محفوظة؟
la tḥātīn, mub sālfa. il-malaffāt maḥfūẓa?
Don't worry, it's no big deal. Are the files saved?
A
هيه، العرض على الإيميل. بس الكيبورد كله مبلول!
hē, il-ʿarẓ ʿala l-īmēl. bas il-kībōrd killah mablūl!
Yes, the presentation's in my email. But the whole keyboard's soaked!
B
عادي، عطيني مناديل. وبفتح العرض على لابتوبي
ʿādi, ʿaṭīni manādīl. w baftaḥ il-ʿarẓ ʿala lābtōbi
No problem, give me some tissues. And I'll open the presentation on my laptop.
A
بس شكلي بيكون مب زين قدام العميل. بكون خجلانة!
bas shakli biykūn mub zēn jiddām il-ʿamīl. bakūn khajlāna!
But I'm going to look bad in front of the client. I'll be so embarrassed!
B
كل شي يهون. العميل ما بيكتشف شي
kill shay yhūn. il-ʿamīl ma biyiktishif shay

الله يستر... وإذا خرب اللابتوب؟ ما أستبعد!
allāh yistur... w idha khirab il-lābtōb? ma astabʿid!

الشركة بتصلحه. خففي على نفسج، مب أول مرة تصير
ish-sharika bitṣallḥah. khaffifi ʿala nafsich, mub awwal marra tṣīr

title: Checkpoint 5.1: Sēf's farewell
goal: Checkpoint: at Bū Rāshid's farewell dinner, Sēf finds Fahad (in from Kuwait); insist you told him so, play down your part, and send Sēf off with blessings
tip: Review, and now you say it: huwa b-nafsah, wallāh il-ʿaẓīm, ashukk inn, iẓ-ẓāhir inn, mub dhāk iz-zōd, shidd ḥēlak, mub sālfa, allāh ysahhil ʿalēk, and send-offs: ṭamminni ʿalēk 'let me know you're OK', dīr bālak ʿala nafsak.
grammar: checkpoint 5.1 (s5u001–s5u014): hedging, insisting, playing down, wishes
dialogue: A
فهد هني؟! يعني مب صدفة، اللي شفته في المول كان هو؟
Fahad hni?! yaʿni mub ṣudfa, illi shiftah fi l-mōl kān huwa?
Fahad's here?! So it was no coincidence; the person you saw at the mall really was him?
B
شفت؟ هو بنفسه! قلت لك، والله العظيم
shift? huwa b-nafsah! gilt-lak, wallāh il-ʿaẓīm
See? The man himself! I told you, I swore it!
A
الظاهر الكل كان يدري إلا أنا. هذا حظي!
iẓ-ẓāhir il-kill kān yadri illa ana. hādha ḥaẓẓi!
Apparently everyone knew except me. Just my luck!
B
هههه، أشك إنك ما كنت تدري! الظاهر إنك على نياتك
hahaha, ashukk innak ma kint tadri! iẓ-ẓāhir innak ʿala nyātak
Haha, I doubt you really didn't know! Looks like you're too trusting.
A
وعمي يقول إنك ساعدت راشد في كل شي. ما قصرت
w ʿammi ygūl innak sāʿadt Rāshid fi kill shay. mā gaṣṣart
And my uncle says you helped Rāshid with everything. Thank you so much.
B
ما سوينا شي. مب ذاك الزود، مب سالفة
mā sawwēna shay. mub dhāk iz-zōd, mub sālfa
It was nothing. Nothing special, no big deal.
A
عساك على القوة. تعال أحضنك، ما أحب الوداع!
ʿasāk ʿala l-gūwa. taʿāl aḥẓnak, ma aḥibb il-wadāʿ!
Well done, and thank you. Come here, let me give you a hug; I hate goodbyes!
B
الله يقويك. ونحن بعد. شد حيلك، الله يسهل عليك وترجع بالسلامة
allāh ygawwīk. w niḥin baʿad. shidd ḥēlak, allāh ysahhil ʿalēk w tirjaʿ bis-salāma
Thanks. Us too. Keep at it; may God make it easy for you, and may you come back safe.
A
آمين، الله يسلمك. وانت بعد شد حيلك في الشغل
āmīn, allāh ysallmak. w inta baʿad shidd ḥēlak fi sh-shughul
Amen, thank you. And you keep at it at work too.
B
إن شاء الله. دير بالك على نفسك، وطمني عليك
in shāʼ allāh. dīr bālak ʿala nafsak, w ṭamminni ʿalēk
God willing. Look after yourself, and let me know you're OK.
